title: Build-a-Bronco
subtitle: A modular 3D-printed SCU mascot, sold at the campus bookstore

maturity.label: Sold through the SCU Campus Bookstore

pitch: A modular, multi-color 3D-printed SCU Bronco mascot whose parts snap together like Lego, designed, fabricated, and sold to a real client in SCU's Applied Entrepreneurship course.
highlights: Designed the main product in CAD across many iterations, including the cross-fit snap-together assembly system
Optimized fabrication in the SCU Maker Lab to mass-produce 25 units
The 25 units sold out in 3 days at the SCU Campus Bookstore (team result)
One of the top-achieving teams in the course

blocks.md: ENGR 172, Applied Entrepreneurship I and II with Dr. Christopher Kitts, has student teams design, fabricate, and sell a real product to a real client. Our client was SCU Athletics and our sales channel was the SCU Campus Bookstore. On a team of 5, I was the Design & Fabrication Engineer: I co-developed the product concept, designed the Bronco in CAD, optimized the geometry for 3D printability (orientation, supports, tolerances), prototyped the print settings, materials, and multi-color strategy in the SCU Maker Lab, and assembled the product.
The 25 units sold out in 3 days at the SCU Campus Bookstore, and ours was one of the top-achieving teams in the course.
